articles.title: As Trump's deadline for a cap on credit card rates looms, banks have only questions and no answers
articles.mainIdea: As Trump's deadline for a cap on credit card rates looms, banks have only questions and no answers
articles.summary: Associated Press Finance: As Trump's deadline for a cap on credit card rates looms, banks have only questions and no answers. President Donald Trump a week ago told the credit card industry it had until Jan. 20 to comply with his demand for a 10% cap on interest rates. With just days to go, consumer groups, politicians, and bankers alike remain unclear on what the White House has planned and whether Trump even remains serious about the idea. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said the president has “an expectation” that credit card companies will accede to his demand that they cap interest rates on credit cards at 10%. Related tickers mentioned: AAPL, GS, JPM, UAL.

articles.summary: Benzinga: Dan Ives Calls It 1996, Not 1999 — 3 AI Stocks Wall Street Still Isn't Pricing In. Dan Ives is pushing back on the market's biggest AI anxiety. As tech earnings kick off, the Wedbush analyst says this isn't a 1999-style excess cycle — it's mid-1996, when spending accelerates, doubts linger, and the biggest gains are still ahead. His message is clear: upcoming results should validate a massive AI buildout that the Street continues to underestimate in both scale and duration.
